note: Newest first. where: live = the normal app, test = the test version (/test/), android = the Android app.

entries.title: PC app: Counter option on Character cards
items: Card templates has a new Counter (left side) section: choose Counter +1000 or +2000 (the lightning icon comes with it). Loading a card from the card list sets its counter automatically.

entries.title: PC app: text colour choices work on your own text
items: Fix: with "Use my text" on, choosing a text colour version (black, white, outlined, golden, red) for Name, Power, Life, Type and Card number now changes your own text instead of the hidden original.

entries.title: PC app: name, power and type colour options now colour your own text
items: Fix: with "Use my text" on, the Card Name Gradient, Power Gradient and Type Gradient options coloured the original EDIT HERE text and did nothing to yours. They now colour your own text (for example red or gold).

entries.title: PC app: two-colour Leader cards
items: The Leader template now has all 15 two-colour looks (Red/Blue, Black/Purple, ...) and the Presets page shows a tile for each. Replace your Leader template with the new OnePiece_Leader_template.psd (Remove this template, then Open another PSD).

entries.title: PC app: card presets page
items: Card templates now opens on a Presets page: a tile for every card type (Character, Leader, Event, Stage, Don) and colour, with a preview picture. Click one and the editor opens with the right layers chosen and every text field empty, ready for your text and art.
Character also has two-colour tiles. The Custom tile opens the editor as before, and a Presets button brings you back.

entries.title: PC app: preview a look by hovering it
items: In Card templates the layer dropdowns now open our own list. Moving the mouse over an option shows it on the card right away; moving away restores the card; clicking picks it.

entries.title: PC app: Card templates options grouped by part of the card
items: The options are now grouped per part of the card, from the top down: Card data, Frame & background, Cost, Power & life, Art, Ability text & trigger, Type, Name, Card number & marks, Extras.
Each part has its text field and its look dropdowns together.

entries.title: PC app: white outline on ability text
items: New "Outline" option in Card templates: black ability text and the coloured pills get a white outline so they stay readable on see-through text boxes over art (on by default).

entries.title: PC app: ability text looks more like the printed cards
items: Ability text uses a medium weight instead of thin, and the (reminder text in brackets) is shown in italics like on real cards.

entries.title: PC app: cost numbers for Event and Stage
items: The Cost field now swaps the real number layer on Event and Stage templates too (new templates with cost 0-10).
The page works out the default cost of each template by itself (4 on Character, 5 on Event and Stage).

entries.title: PC app: 5-digit power keeps real proportions
items: Power of 10000 and up is now drawn slightly smaller with the same proportions (measured on a real card), instead of being squeezed sideways.

entries.title: PC app: 5-digit power fits the frame
items: Power of 10000 and up is squeezed sideways so it no longer touches the frame corner, like on real cards.

entries.title: PC app: number layers hidden from the layer dropdowns
items: The ready-made number layers (power 6000, cost 7 ...) are no longer listed in the layer dropdowns. Type the number in the Power / Cost fields instead.

entries.title: PC app: real card numbers for cost and power
items: Card templates has a new Cost field. When the template has a ready-made layer for the number you type, the card uses it (same look as the real card) instead of drawn text.
Works with the new Character template that includes cost 0-10 and power 0-13000 layers. Other card types follow.
Saved PSDs also contain the right number layers.

entries.title: PC app: click a text on the card to type it
items: In Card templates you can now click the name, power, type, card number or ability on the card and type right there.
The hint no longer sends you to Photoshop: the PNG already has your text.

entries.title: PC app: easier updating
items: New "Update Nightvault" button at the bottom of the side menu.
The update check now tries three download addresses (GitHub, GitHub Pages, jsDelivr) and shows the reason when none answers.
New "Update from a zip file": pick Nightvault-PC-latest.zip and the program updates itself, for PCs that cannot reach GitHub.

entries.title: PC app: card templates handle Don cards
items: Card templates page no longer draws an ability text on templates that have no ability box (Don cards).

entries.title: PC app: card stays in place, sections and highlight in Card templates
items: The card preview now stays on screen while you scroll the list of editable parts.
The edit options are split into sections (Frame & layers, Text, Art) that can be folded.
When you click or hover a field or dropdown, the matching zone on the card is highlighted in yellow.

entries.title: PC app: card templates handle Event cards
items: Card templates page now handles templates without a power number or other text parts (like Event cards): parts the template does not have are simply not drawn.

entries.title: PC app: card templates work for Leaders too
items: The text editor now follows the layout of whichever template is open (Character or Leader), with a Life field for Leaders.
Fixes a rare error when switching templates while the card was still drawing.

entries.title: PC app: card templates get a text and art editor
items: Card templates page: type the name, power, type, card number and ability text; tags like [blue|Activate: Main], [pink|Once Per Turn], [orange|Rush] and [black|DON!! x1] become coloured labels; text auto-fits the box.
Choose your own art and move/zoom it behind the frame.
Load card data: type a card number or name and it fills the fields from an offline One Piece card list (press Update list once; needs internet).
Roboto and Roboto Condensed (free fonts) are included. If the fonts do not show after one update, press Check for updates a second time.

entries.title: PC app: Card templates page
items: New Tools > Card templates page: open a layered card PSD (for example the merged One Piece Character template), choose each layer version with dropdowns, see the card, and save a PNG or a PSD with exactly those layers switched on.
Text on the card stays as in the file for now; edit it in Photoshop or GIMP after saving. Needs 8-bit RGB PSD files. Update the PC app from Settings > Updates.

entries.title: PC app: Updates panel at the top of Settings
items: Check for updates now sits in its own Updates panel at the top of Settings and shows the result in a window instead of a short message.

entries.title: PC app: update check fixed
items: A failed update check no longer blocks new tries for a day, so the update bar shows up as soon as the connection works.

entries.title: Translate One Piece cards (Dutch for the kids) + OPPP key on the PC
items: Proxies menu › Translate One Piece cards: with your OPPP supporter key, the One Piece cards of your deck are redrawn in another language (Dutch first in the list, 28 languages in all). The name, type and ability text are machine-translated, so check them. Each card takes about half a minute because OPPP draws them one at a time. The result is added to your deck as your own picture. You can also type card codes like OP01-001.

The PC app can download One Piece in full resolution with your OPPP key (game One Piece (OPPP, full resolution); key in Settings › Card games › OPPP key), alternate arts included. The PC updates itself: tap Update now when the bar appears.
Your key stays on the device or PC only and is never shown in logs or messages. Not tried on a real device yet.

entries.title: One Piece: full-resolution cards with your OPPP key
items: Card pictures › One Piece (OPPP) has a new field for your OPPP supporter key. With it you get the full-resolution cards (1800 x 2516 pixels) and the alternate arts (in an Alternate art folder). Without a key it works like before (417 x 582).

The key stays on your device only: it is not in backups, and it is hidden from the debug log and error messages. The app checks it with one small request before downloading and tells you if OPPP refuses it.
Full-size cards are about 3-4 MB each, so tick WebP to save space. Not tried on a real device yet.

entries.title: Card pictures: One Piece from OPPP (mostly without watermark)
items: Card pictures has a second One Piece source, One Piece (OPPP - mostly without watermark), from a fan proxy site. The pictures are 417 x 582 pixels: readable and fine for casual proxies, but smaller than a high-resolution scan.
It saves into its own folder (onepiece-oppp), only the normal art of each card, and goes slowly to be kind to the small site.
Not tried on a real device yet.

entries.title: PC app: updates itself
items: The PC app now checks once a day if a newer version is available and shows a bar with Update now. Settings has a Check for updates button.
Updating replaces only Nightvault's own program files, keeps the old ones in the update_backup folder and restarts by itself. Your data is never touched.
Install this version by hand once (copy the new files); after that it updates itself.

entries.title: Check for new cards (ongoing games only)
items: Download many games has a new button, Check for new cards. It only looks at games that are still being printed and downloads the sets that are not in your folder yet, plus the two newest sets (they often get cards added).

Every game has a tag: ongoing or legacy (no longer in print). Tap it to switch. Legacy games are skipped. Starting legacy list: WoW, Dragon Ball Z CCG and GT, Star Wars CCG, Dragon Ball Z TCG and all the old CCG Trader games.
The PC app has the same tags and button (copy vault.py and vault_ui.html again). Not tried on a real device yet.

entries.title: PC app: download many games at once, converted to WebP
items: Cards page: new button Download many games. Tick the games (untick the ones you already have, it remembers), choose a folder such as your SD card or a big drive, and it downloads every set of each game and converts each game to WebP before starting the next, so the disk never fills with huge originals.
Settings › Card games: new button Add all games that have pictures (the CCG Trader games, except Magic, Pokémon and Yu-Gi-Oh!).
Install: copy vault.py, vault_ui.html, vault_tcgdata.py and vault_ccgtrader.py to your PC and restart Nightvault. Not tried on your PC yet.

entries.title: Card pictures: download many games at once
items: New button in Card pictures: Download many games at once. Tick the games and it goes through all their sets by itself, one game after the other.

Untick the games you already have - the app remembers it. Pictures already in your folder are never downloaded twice, so Stop and start again is safe. Games that already have a folder in your chosen folder are marked.
Magic and Pokémon can be saved at the largest size (PNG) or the normal size. Not tried on a real device yet; plan for a lot of space.

entries.title: Card scanner: add all CCG Trader games that have pictures
items: Settings › Card games has a new button: Add all games that have pictures. It puts about 260 more card games in your game list in one go (Magic, Pokémon and Yu-Gi-Oh! are skipped, they have their own lists). They are tucked into one folded group so the list stays easy to read.
Changed your mind? Remove the ones added together takes them out again. Games you already have cards in stay.
Card pictures (Proxies menu): CCG Trader games without any pictures no longer show up in its list.

entries.title: Card pictures: all the other CCG Trader games
items: The Game list in Card pictures (Proxies menu) now ends with More games from CCG Trader: about 290 older and smaller card games, each saved in its own folder (ccgtrader - game name / set / card).
The pictures are the best size CCG Trader has. Some games have no pictures there, so their set list is empty.
Magic, Yu-Gi-Oh! and Pokémon are not in that group because they have better sources above. Not tried on a real phone yet.

entries.title: Card pictures: Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Hearthstone, WoW, Dragon Ball Z CCG and GT
items: Card pictures (Proxies menu) can now download Pokémon (JPG or PNG), Yu-Gi-Oh!, Hearthstone, World of Warcraft TCG, Dragon Ball Z CCG and Dragon Ball GT, into the same game / set / card folders as the other games.
Works with the WebP option and with an SD card folder. Never tried on a real phone yet: if a game fails, send the debug log.

PC app: new button Convert to WebP on a game page (any folder, also your SD card): makes the pictures much smaller, keeps or removes the originals, and continues where it stopped. Copy vault.py and vault_ui.html to your PC.

entries.title: Proxies: Save the PDF to your Downloads folder
items: After Make PDF the app now shows "Your file is ready" with two buttons: Save to Downloads (puts the PDF in your phone's Downloads folder, find it in your Files app) and Share or send (opens Android's share menu, for mail, WhatsApp, a printer app). Before, only the share menu opened, which has no way to save on the phone.
Needs Android 10 or newer for Save to Downloads.

entries.title: Proxies: the sheet preview shows the bleed as it will print
items: With bleed on, the preview used to show a pink box around every card (a marker, not the real fill). It now shows the card picture extending into the bleed (or black / white, as you chose). The PDF itself was already right; only the preview changed. The preview stretches the whole picture a little, the PDF stretches the edges.

entries.title: Proxies: Pokémon deck lists with numbers in brackets
items: Deck lines like "4 Dreepy (71)" or "3 Basic Psychic Energy (5)" are now read as card number 71 / 5, not as a set code, so the card is found by its name.
For Pokémon, a trailing [name] such as "Boss's Orders [Ghetsis]" is ignored. "Sol Ring (CMD) 123" and "Lightning Bolt (M11)" still mean set (and number).

entries.title: Proxies: several card makers (Card Conjurer, Yugilife ...)
items: The Card maker screen can now hold several tools. Add each one under a name (for example Card Conjurer, Yugilife) and choose its folder - the one with index.html. Each opens inside Proxies on its own address, and cards you save in any of them are added to your deck as your own pictures.
Nightvault still includes none of these tools or their frames: you download or build them yourself. A tool that has to be built first (Yugilife) must be built on a PC; add the built website folder.
Menu name is now "Card makers (your own offline copies)". Android app only, not tried with real tools yet.

entries.title: Proxies: Card maker (open your own offline card maker)
items: New in the Proxies menu: Card maker. It opens an offline card maker (for example Card Conjurer) from a folder on your phone. Nightvault does not include one - you download the files yourself, copy the folder to the phone and choose the folder that contains index.html.
It runs on its own address, so it cannot read Nightvault's data. Cards you save in it (picture downloads) are added to your deck as your own pictures; other files (save files) go to Save / Share.
Android app only. First version, never tried with the real files yet: if something does not load, send the debug log.

entries.title: Proxies: print from the pictures saved on your phone
items: New switch in Sheet details: "Use pictures saved on this phone first". When you saved card pictures with Card pictures, Proxies takes them from the folder instead of downloading them again, and only asks the internet for cards you did not save.
After the PDF is made it says how many pictures came from the phone and how many from the internet.
Works for the games in Card pictures (Magic, Lorcana, Star Wars: Unlimited, One Piece ...). JPG and WebP files both work. Finding a card by name still needs the internet for now.
Not tried on a real phone yet.

entries.title: Proxies: Community art (MPC Autofill)
items: Tap a card in Proxies, then "Search community art": proxy art made by the MPC Autofill artists, shown with the artist, the DPI and the file size. Pick one and it goes on your sheet and is saved with the deck.
Android app only (the MPC server only talks to its own website in a browser).
First version, not tried on the real server yet: if it says it could not reach MPC Autofill, send the debug log. Downloading a whole artist and "check for new cards" come later.

entries.title: Card pictures: save as WebP while downloading
items: New choice in Card pictures: "Save pictures as" - As the site has them (JPG/PNG) or WebP. With WebP the phone converts every picture while it saves it, so the folder ends up about 3-5 times smaller and the pictures look the same.
The size shown before you start is adjusted for WebP. Pictures that already come as WebP are saved as they are.
Proxies can print WebP pictures. Note: PC folders hold JPG, so a WebP folder is not identical to the PC layout (file ends in .webp).

entries.title: Card pictures: Star Wars Unlimited, One Piece, Star Wars CCG, Riftbound
items: Card pictures (Proxies ☰ › Card pictures) now also saves Star Wars: Unlimited, One Piece, Star Wars CCG and Riftbound.

Star Wars: Unlimited gets one folder per version inside every set: Normal, Hyperspace, Showcase, Prestige, Serialized and so on (whatever the official list has). Foil and Hyperspace Foil are the same picture as Normal and Hyperspace, so they are not saved twice.
Not tested on the real sites yet (my test only used pretend answers). If a set stays empty, send the debug log.

entries.title: Proxies: example for "Card name x3"
items: The deck box now also shows the "Card name x3" way of typing copies as an example.

entries.title: Proxies: "Wellwisher x5" now works
items: Typing a number after the name (Wellwisher x5) is now read as 5 copies, not as part of the name. Before, the app searched for a card called "Wellwisher x5" and found nothing.
Adding one card by name also accepts 4 Lightning Bolt or 2x Sol Ring.

entries.title: Card pictures on the phone (first part)
items: New: save card pictures on your phone, like the PC downloaders do. Open Proxies, tap the menu (three lines) and choose Card pictures. Pick a folder once (also the SD card), then a game and the sets you want.
The pictures land in the same folders and names as on the PC (game / set / number_name.jpg), so a folder can be copied between the PC and the phone. A download you stop continues where it was.
First games: Magic (small, normal, large or PNG, the size is shown first), Lorcana, Gundam, Digimon, Flesh and Blood, Sorcery, Weiss Schwarz and Dragon Ball. The other games follow. Android app only.
Using the saved pictures in Proxies (printing offline), copying sets from your PC, and Binder come in later updates.

entries.title: Proxies: finding cards by name is more reliable
items: Adding a card by name now also finds it when you type only part of the name ('deathr' finds Deathrite Shaman) or make a small typo.
The name boxes no longer let the phone keyboard 'correct' card names like Deathrite or Wellwisher.
When the card site can't be reached, or says to wait a moment, the app now says so (and the card shows 'Could not load - tap to try again') instead of saying the card was not found.

entries.title: New app: Proxies – print a deck as proxy cards
items: A new tile in The Nightvault: paste a deck list, pick the art of every card, and get a PDF sheet with cut marks. It works on the phone and in the browser, the PDF is made on your device and nothing is uploaded.
Every game Pocket knows has its card size ready (63×88, Yu-Gi-Oh 59×86 …), plus common sizes and your own size.
Tap a card to choose another printing or use your own picture. Bleed, gap, cut marks, 150–600 dpi, double-faced cards and mirrored card-back pages for double-sided printing.
Saved decks stay on this device. Decks from Pocket, your binder and deck-site links, and our own card design come in the next updates.

entries.title: Bookcase: set-up steps for Metron, Google Drive and Flemish comics
items: The next time Bookcase opens it shows what's new: the Metron account (with where to sign up), books from Google Drive with Sign in with Google, and the album lists for Flemish and Dutch comics. Also under the ? button.

entries.title: Bookcase: Metron, and Sign in with Google for Drive
items: Metron (metron.cloud), a free comics database made by fans, is now a source next to Comic Vine, GCD and Wikipedia: series, every issue with its cover, reading orders (story arcs) and what came out this week. Shelf ⚙ → Online → Metron account (free account, Android app).
Discover shows new releases from Metron when you have no Comic Vine key (or tap “from … ⇄” to switch).

Google Drive: Sign in with Google (Add → From Google Drive, or shelf ⚙ → Google Drive folders). Google trusts a signed-in account much more than the key, so it pauses downloads far less. Needs the setup in Google's console first.

entries.title: New app: Collectables
items: Collectables is here: anything you collect, each collection with its own template – you choose the fields every item gets (text, number, money, date, year, yes/no, a list to pick from, a link). Start from Coins, Stamps, Vinyl figures, Building sets, Die-cast cars, Figures, Trading pins, Watches, Fossils & minerals, or empty.
Items have photos, notes, tags, how many and a barcode. With 'Track prices' on, you see what you paid, what it is worth now, and the total of the collection.
The camera has Photo and Barcode mode. A scanned barcode looks up the name and a picture in free product lists, and tells you when you already have it. Text and Recognise come later.
Groups like Music: items with the same value in a field you choose (Country, Series …) make one tile; your own groups, groups inside groups, pins.
Install it from The Nightvault › Add more Nightvault apps. Photos are not in the automatic backup.

entries.title: Calendar: board games
items: Calendar has a Board games chip with upcoming board games and miniatures from the boardgamesnmore.com release schedule (about 7 months ahead). Only the month is known, so each shows on the 1st of its month. Android app only.

entries.title: Calendar: new books; green glow in more apps
items: Calendar: a Books chip with new books by the writers on your Books shelf (up to 100, from Google Books; only exact dates). Open Bookcase once after this update.
The green glow on new items now also works in Games, Boardgames, 3D Print and Audiobooks (Audiobooks: single books; groups do not glow yet).

entries.title: Calendar: new albums of your artists
items: The Calendar has a Music chip: new albums and EPs coming in the next 60 days from the artists in your Music app (up to your 150 biggest), from MusicBrainz. No key needed.
Open Music once after this update so the Calendar learns your artists.

entries.title: Calendar: your own iCal links
items: Calendar ☰ → Calendar links (iCal): paste a link such as your Otaku Calendar feed and its releases show under "My links" next to everything else (repeating events too).
Links are read inside the Android app only.

entries.title: New: Calendar
items: A new Calendar tile in The Nightvault (it appears by itself) shows what is coming out in the next 60 days: movies, series, comics, games and manga, without adding anything first.
Filter per kind, tap the heart to follow something. A follow that comes out within 3 days gives the Calendar tile a green dot.
Movies and series use your TMDB key from Cinema, comics your Comic Vine key from Bookcase (Android app only). Games need a free RAWG key: ☰ → Keys.
Books and board games are not in yet: no good source was found.

entries.title: Tablets: more tiles in a row
items: On a tablet or wide window the tiles in The Nightvault keep the same size as on a phone and simply fit more per row (before it stayed at 3).

entries.title: Translate the bubbles (new Android app build)
items: Read along bar › globe (or ⚙ › Translate the bubbles…): pick a language and download it once (about 30 MB, free, works offline afterwards).
The translation shows as a caption under the bubble you are on; tap the caption to see the original.
The translation can be read aloud in the voice of that language. Bubbles that carry on in the next bubble are translated together.
Translated pages are kept per book, so a page is never translated twice. This needs the new Android app: install the update.

entries.title: Panel by panel and scrolling strips
items: New panel button in the reader: the screen zooms to one panel at a time. Auto moves on by itself, Manual waits for your tap.
Works on odd pages too: it looks for gutters, then panel outlines, then follows the speech bubbles (Android), and falls back to the whole page.
With Read along on, only the bubbles of the panel on screen are read.
Long strips (Infinity Comics, webtoons) open as one scrolling column; Panels scrolls them step by step. Switch per book or per series in ⚙ › Reading style.
Wrong cut? ⚙ › Fix the panels on this page: move, draw, delete boxes and tap them in the order you want. Fixes can be shared as a small file.
Sound effects are skipped by default; switch them on in ⚙.

entries.title: Read along: panel by panel order
items: Read along now finds the panels on the page (the empty strips between them) and reads panel after panel, left to right, top to bottom; the bubbles inside a panel in order.
Before, a bubble that sat a little higher in the right panel was read first, which felt like reading right to left.
Changing a comic's reading direction while Read along is on now takes effect straight away.

entries.title: Faster natural voices
items: Four new natural English voices that are fast on almost every phone: Lessac and Ryan (US), Alba and Northern English (British) - 21 MB each, in the voice screen.
Read along makes the next bubbles while one is being read (also the first ones of the next page), and gets the voice ready while it reads the page, so there are fewer pauses.
Kokoro sounds nicest but is slow on most phones; the voice screen now says which voices are fast, and Read along shows when the voice is still getting ready.

entries.title: Natural voices easier to find
items: Read along now offers the natural voice itself the first time: one tap on Download, and the bubbles are read in Kokoro's voice.
The Read along bar has a voice button: download voices, pick the voice for English and Dutch, play a sample.
Audiobooks › ⚙ › Read-aloud voice shows the Download buttons straight away (no tab to find first).

entries.title: Read along: comics and manga read aloud
items: In a comic or manga, tap the speech-bubble button at the top: the bubbles are read aloud one by one and light up, then the page turns by itself.
Tap a bubble to hear that one. Auto: it carries on from there. Tap only: it reads just the bubbles you tap - handy for wild page layouts.
Pause, next bubble and speed in the bar at the bottom. The voice is the one you picked in Audiobooks (⚙ › Read-aloud voice), also the natural voices.

entries.title: Natural voices for reading aloud, in the app
items: Audiobooks → ⚙ → Read-aloud voice → Natural voices: tap Download for Kokoro (English, 11 voices) or Nathalie / Pim (Dutch). Once - then it works without internet, no extra app needed.
The first time you listen to an EPUB, Audiobooks offers the natural voice itself: one tap.
Pick the voice for English and for Dutch books, and play a sample. The phone's own voices are still there too.

entries.title: Listen to EPUBs as audiobooks
items: Bookcase: an EPUB has a Listen button (also book ⋯ → Listen as audiobook). It opens in Audiobooks and is read aloud by your phone's voice.
You get the whole audiobook player: chapters from the book, it remembers where you were, speed, sleep timer, bookmarks, lock screen.
Audiobooks → Settings → Read-aloud voice: pick the voice engine and the voice for English and Dutch books, and listen to a sample.
For a natural voice: install a voice app (for example a Kokoro voice app), then pick it there. A built-in natural voice comes later.

entries.title: First start: a live demo for every app
items: Every app page in the new first start now has a small looping demo of a real feature: binder pockets filling, pictures shrinking, a NEW tag then the reader, a tile moving into a group, speed and sleep in the audiobook player, resuming a film, BoardGameGeek sync, a 3D model turning, a wishlist heart.

entries.title: Boardgames: says why BGG games are missing
items: When the daily BoardGameGeek update can't run (for example the BGG user name and token are not set on GitHub yet, or BGG refuses the token), Boardgames now says why on its first page and in Settings.
No more daily "failed" e-mails while the BGG user name and token are simply not set yet.

entries.title: First start: Scanner shows a live scan demo
items: On the Scanner page of the new first start, a small viewfinder shows a card being scanned and the name, number and price fields lining up. The other apps still have simple animations for now.

entries.title: New first-start: one page per app
items: A fresh install now walks you through the apps, one full-screen page each: what it does, a small animation, and a tick to take it.
Previous, Skip and Next at the bottom. Next only works once you ticked the app; Skip goes on without it.
The last page shows what will be installed, then installs only those apps.

entries.title: Green glow: Bookcase series and re-added items
items: Bookcase: a series or book tile glows when it has books that are new to the app (before, only the lists did, so series tiles never glowed).
If you delete something and add it again, it is new again and glows.
Bookcase starts fresh with this update: what is in it now does not glow. Delete and re-add a series to see it.

entries.title: Camera starts on the back camera
items: The scanner sometimes opened the selfie camera when you started it. It now remembers whether you use the back or the front camera, and goes back to the rear camera unless you picked the front one yourself (flip button or Settings).

entries.title: Bookcase: NEW tags go away when you have looked
items: Opening a series, one of its books, or reading it now takes the NEW tag off the shelf tile. Inside the series page the new issues stay marked while you look at them.
Opening a single issue also clears its own NEW tag.

entries.title: Bookcase: the new-issues block is folded
items: The big red "series with new issues" block is now one slim line. Tap it to show or hide the list of series. "Check now" stays next to it.

entries.title: New things glow
items: New items in Bookcase, Cinema and Music (from a scan of your SD card, a PC sync or added by hand) get a green glow.
The 24 hours start when you first open the app and see them; the glow also stops as soon as you open the item.
What you already have when you first update does not glow.

entries.title: Dots inside the apps
items: The ☰ button of every app now shows the same dot as its tile in The Nightvault (orange = backup is old, blue = news or update, green = something new).
Open the ☰ menu and the top lines tell you why the dot is there.

entries.title: Blue dots only when there is really something
items: On Android the blue dot stayed on every tile even with the newest build. Now it shows only when a newer Android build exists or an app has news you have not seen yet.
Opening an app, or reading What's new, now reliably clears its news dot.

entries.title: The ☰ menu works in Music and Audiobooks
items: The ☰ menu was covered by a dark layer in Music and Audiobooks, so it looked dim and could not be tapped. It now sits on top and works. The same safeguard is in every app.

entries.title: Convert and Control: back goes to The Nightvault
items: On Android, the back button in Convert and Control now returns to The Nightvault (first it closes the ☰ menu if that is open). Before, nothing happened.

entries.title: The ☰ menu always fits on the screen
items: The ☰ menu in every app is now kept fully on screen. In Music it used to run off the left edge so the words could not be read.

entries.title: Bookcase: you can see where the new dot comes from
items: The shelves on Bookcase's home page now show a red NEW badge with a number when a series inside has new volumes or issues, so you can tap straight to it.
The Nightvault's 'New in your apps' list now names the series (for example 'Berserk (2)').

entries.title: Every app: ☰ menu, new splash screen and the Nightvault themes
items: Every app now has a ☰ menu in the top bar instead of the settings icon: The Nightvault (back home), the app's own extras, Settings, How to use & set up, and Back up this app now. Cinema's calendar and 3D Print's Prints moved into it.
Every app follows the theme you pick in The Nightvault (☰ > All themes & colours): dark, light, the new Gold, Rose and Sand, or your own colours. The theme is only chosen in the hub.

The splash screen is back in every app and says 'Nightvault' plus the name of the app that opens (Scanner, Binder, Music …), with its icon in the app's colour from your theme. One switch for all apps in the hub's Appearance screen; tap the splash to skip it.
Scanner and Binder: the old theme list in Settings is gone (colours come from The Nightvault now) and the header says Scanner or Binder instead of Pocket.

entries.title: Swipe through scan templates
items: On the scan screen, swipe left or right on the camera picture to switch between the scan templates of the chosen game (Standard and your own). A short message says which one is on.
The dashed boxes move to where that template reads the name and number, and the scanner tries the template you picked first. It is remembered per game.

entries.title: The Nightvault: tile icons follow the theme
items: With ☰ > All themes & colours > 'Apps keep their own colour' switched off, all tile icons take the theme's colour. Switched on, each app keeps its own colour. An app with its own theme (Each app) uses that theme's colour.

entries.title: Bookcase and Cinema tell The Nightvault what is new
items: When Bookcase finds new volumes or issues, or Cinema has a show with something new, the tile on The Nightvault home screen gets a green dot and the item appears under ☰ > New in your apps.

entries.title: The Nightvault: square tiles, a menu and themes
items: The home screen now shows your apps as square tiles, three across, so you see more without scrolling.
A small glowing dot on a tile tells you something: green = something new in the app, blue = an update or news, orange = needs attention (like an old backup).
The buttons at the top are gone from the header and live in the ☰ menu: My PC, Backups, Apps & updates, New in your apps, Arrange tiles, Add more apps, Dark/Light and Debug mode.

New Appearance screen (☰ > All themes & colours): 10 themes including the new Gold, Rose and Sand, a light/dark switch, and 'Your own colours' where you pick 4 colours and it warns when text is hard to read.
For now only The Nightvault itself follows the theme; the other apps will join one by one.

entries.title: Every app: set-up and how to use
items: The first time you open an app, a short tour shows what it does and how to use it, and helps you set it up: the free keys it can use (TMDB, IGDB, Steam, Comic Vine …) with a link to where you get them and the steps, your PC, Tailscale. Skip anything and do it later.
The new “?” button next to ⚙ in every app shows the tour and set-up again.
After an update that adds something new to set up or worth explaining, the app shows just that, once (“New in …”).

entries.title: Cinema calendar: full details when you open something
items: Tapping a film or series in “Everything coming” (or the next film of a series) now opens a full page in Cinema instead of a link: poster, story, rating, genres, length, director and cast, the trailer, the release dates in Belgium (with “in 12 days”), the next episode and where to watch it in Belgium.
♥ Want to see right there - and when it is already in Cinema, “Open in Cinema”.

entries.title: Cinema calendar: everything that is coming
items: The calendar has a second tab: “Everything coming” – no need to add films and shows one by one.
In cinemas: every film coming to Belgian cinemas. Streaming: films coming to streaming. Series: popular series with a new episode or season soon. Popular now: what everyone watches this week.
Pick a genre, and set your streaming services (⚙ → Calendar → My streaming services, e.g. only Netflix and Disney+) so Streaming and Series only show what you can watch.
Tap ♥ to put one on your want-to-see list, or “Select several” to tick many and add them all at once. They then appear under “My films & shows” with reminders.

entries.title: Cinema: the calendar is easier to find
items: A calendar button (📅) at the top of Cinema, on every page, opens “Coming soon”.
The Coming soon row on Cinema's start page now always shows - without a TMDB key it tells you to add one (⚙ → TMDB), which the calendar needs for its dates.

entries.title: Cinema: Coming soon – the calendar
items: New in Cinema: “Coming soon”. The start page shows what is coming in the next weeks; tap Calendar › for everything, as a list by week or as a month.
It shows new episodes of your shows, the next film of a film series you have (like a new Shrek), and the films and shows on your new “want to see” list.

Want to see: Calendar → ♥ Want to see…, search a film or show. It gets its own shelf, shows its release dates for Belgium (in cinemas, streaming & buy, DVD & Blu-ray – Dutch dates when Belgium has none) and where to watch it in Belgium.
A reminder on your phone on the day (at 9:00 – change it or switch it off in ⚙ → Calendar, or tap 🔔 to stop it for one show). Tap the reminder to open it.
Shows with an episode that came out since you last watched get a NEW EP mark.
Uses your TMDB key; the dates are looked up twice a day when you open Cinema.

entries.title: Every app comes back where you were
items: Music, Audiobooks, Cinema, Games, Boardgames and 3D Print now also put back the screen you were on (a shelf, an album, a game page …) when Android closed The Nightvault in the background and you open it again within 3 hours.

entries.title: Back where you were after switching apps
items: When Android closes The Nightvault in the background and you open it again, it now goes straight back to the app you were in instead of the home screen (within 3 hours).
Bookcase also puts back the screens you had open and the book you were reading, at your page.

entries.title: Bookcase: gentler with Google Drive
items: When Google pauses downloads (its "Sorry… unusual traffic" robot check), Bookcase says so in plain words and stops asking for half an hour, so the pause doesn't last longer.
Looking through a big Drive folder now goes a bit slower on purpose, so Google doesn't think it's a robot.

entries.title: Bookcase: Google's own reason when Drive refuses a book
items: When Google Drive refuses to send a book, Bookcase now shows Google's own reason (and writes it in the 🐞 log), so we can see what is going on.

entries.title: Bookcase: Google Drive books open in the Android app
items: In the Android app, books on Google Drive are now read through Android's own connection. Before, opening or adding them got stuck ("Google Drive could not be reached"), while the list and covers worked.
Download to this phone fetches big books in parts of 8 MB and shows how far it is.

entries.title: Bookcase: adding a big Google Drive folder works better
items: Adding from Google Drive no longer opens every big PDF to make its cover: it uses Drive's own picture, and books without one get their cover the first time you open them. Much faster for 1000s of books.
Picture folders on Drive use Drive's small picture for the cover too.
One file that doesn't answer can no longer stop the whole import: after 3 minutes it is skipped and the rest goes on. The log (🐞) now shows the progress every 25 books.

entries.title: Bookcase: books from your Google Drive
items: Add → From Google Drive: paste the link of one of your Drive folders (shared with “Anyone with the link”). Bookcase looks through it and all folders inside and fills the shelf, with covers – nothing is downloaded yet.
Books open straight from Drive (only the pages you look at are fetched). Book ⋯ → Download to this phone keeps a copy for offline reading and printing; Select several to download them at once.
Shelf ⚙ → Google Drive folders: look again for new books, stop using a folder, or change your Google key (asked once, kept on this phone).

entries.title: Cinema: play on your TV, watch away from home, subtitles found online
items: Play on TV: ⋯ → Play on TV (or the TV button in the player). The phone finds your Samsung, LG or other TV on the Wi‑Fi and tells it what to play - the TV fetches the film itself in full quality (this is not screen casting). The phone becomes the remote.
Subtitles on the TV: Samsung shows the subtitle file itself; on LG and other TVs your PC puts them in the picture. Dutch first, else English.
A film saved on your phone can play on a friend's TV too - the phone sends it to the TV.

Watch your PC's films away from home: install the free Tailscale app on the PC and on your phone (same account) - Cinema finds the PC by itself. Away it plays in 720p to save data; pick Original, 1080p, 720p or 480p in the player's ⚙ or in Cinema ⚙.

Subtitles found online: set up your free OpenSubtitles account once (Cinema ⚙ → Subtitles online). When a film has no Dutch or English subtitles, the PC finds them, lines them up with the film's sound and keeps them next to the video. Or tap Subtitles → Find online.
Subtitles a bit early or late? Subtitles → Earlier / Later 0.5 s - remembered per film. Subtitles are now on by default.
Needs the newest PC app files: vault.py, vault_phone.py and the new vault_cinema.py.

entries.title: Bookcase + PC: overnight check for new volumes
items: The PC app now looks every night for new volumes (manga: MangaDex and AniList) and issues (comics: GCD) of the series in your library and marks them with a red NEW on the PC cards.
On the phone, Add → From my PC shows the same NEW marks and which numbers are not on the PC yet. 'Check the PC for new releases' starts a check right away.
PC install needed: copy vault.py, vault_phone.py, vault_news.py and vault_ui.html from the private source repo to the PC and restart Nightvault.

entries.title: Bookcase: NEW marks for new volumes and issues
items: Once a day (and with Check now) Bookcase looks online for new volumes or issues of the series on your collection lists.
Series with something new get a bold red NEW tile, a bar on top lists them, and inside the series the new volumes are marked. Tap Seen, or just add the book, and the mark goes away.
Tiles also show how many are still missing.

entries.title: Bookcase: take comics, manga and books from your PC
items: New: Add → From my PC shows the comics, manga, books and RPG books of the Nightvault PC app, with their covers.
Save a series to the phone for offline reading: book by book, a range like 1-12, 15, or the full series. Books you already have are marked.
PC install needed: copy vault.py and vault_phone.py from the private source repo to the PC and restart Nightvault.

entries.title: Bookcase: manga covers load reliably
items: The grey covers of a long manga series no longer stop after about 14 volumes: the app now fetches them one by one, makes them small and keeps them on the phone.
Once a cover has been shown it also appears without internet (for example on a work wifi that blocks MangaDex).
If MangaDex or AniList can't be reached, the message now says a work or school wifi may block them and suggests mobile data.

entries.title: Bookcase: manga get the whole series
items: Manga now work like comics: open a manga series and you see every volume – the ones you have in colour, the ones you don't have grey.
Volume covers come from MangaDex, and the story, writer, artist, genres and status from AniList. No key needed, and only official volumes are used.
After you add manga, Bookcase offers to look them up. You can also pick a series by hand (a book's ⋯ → Look up online, or Collection lists → + Add a series, with MangaDex or AniList).

Collection lists, "Up next" (a grey tile when the next volume is missing) and "Find it" (Google, plus BookWalker and bol.com if you add them) work for manga too. Mark volumes you have on paper with the P badge.
On your own shelves you can switch what the shelf holds (Comics or Manga) in the shelf's settings → Online.
Books (Open Library / Hardcover) come next.

entries.title: Boardgames: files per game
items: Every game now has a Files section: add the rulebook, errata / FAQ, player aids, scenarios or fan-made files you downloaded.
Boardgames guesses what each file is from its name (Rulebook, Errata, Fan-made …); tap ⋯ to change it, rename it, share a copy or remove it.
PDFs, EPUBs, comics and pictures open in Bookcase's reader (zoom, search inside PDFs, bookmarks, print); closing it brings you back to the game. They do not show up on Bookcase's shelves.
Text files open right away; other files (like a 3D model) can be shared to another app.
"Files on BGG" opens the game's files page on BoardGameGeek, to find new fan-made files.
The list of files is in the automatic backups too (the files themselves stay on the phone).

entries.title: Automatic backups of every app
items: Every app now makes a backup of its lists by itself every few days: songs, playlists, favourites, play counts, groups, books, games, plays, films, models and your cards.

The Nightvault → the shield button → Backups: choose a backups folder once (best a new folder “Nightvault backups” on the SD card). A copy is saved there too, so the backups survive even removing the app.
When an app opens empty while a backup has things in it, it asks: “Put it back?” Only what is missing is added.
In Backups you can also back up everything now, and put back any backup of any app (add what is missing, or make it exactly like the backup).
Not in a backup: the files themselves (they stay in your folders), pictures and covers (found again) and your own API keys.

entries.title: All apps: an SD card that isn't ready no longer looks like an empty folder
items: When a phone folder can't be reached (SD card out or not ready yet), the apps now get “can't be reached right now” instead of “no files”, so looking for changes can't remove your songs, books, films or models by mistake.

entries.title: Music: one bad folder look can no longer empty your library
items: When “Look for changes” finds far fewer songs than before (SD card out or not ready, folder renamed, permission lost), Music no longer removes them by itself. It asks first, and “Keep them” is the safe choice.

entries.title: Bookcase: Up next and Reading orders
items: Up next: a row on the home screen and on each shelf with the next comic of every series you're reading. When the next number is one you don't have yet, it shows grey – tap it to find it.

Reading orders: a new tab next to Collection lists. Find a big story or event (Secret Wars, House of X, Court of Owls …) on Comic Vine and see all its issues in the order to read them, across all series – yours in colour, the others grey, with a Read next button.

entries.title: Android app: asks for less (Google Play Protect)
items: Google Play Protect blocked the last Android update. The app had started asking to see every installed app (for Games' emulator buttons) – together with screen capture that looks suspicious to Google.
Now the app only asks about the emulators Games knows (RetroArch, PPSSPP, Dolphin, DuckStation …). Everything works the same.

entries.title: Bookcase: names like “De Rode Ridder -001- Title” make a series
items: File names with the number between dashes (De Rode Ridder -001- Het gebroken zwaard) are now read as series + album number, so they bundle into one series tile and get the full album list with the missing ones grey.
Comics you already added are read again once by themselves when Bookcase starts.

entries.title: Bookcase: Flemish and Dutch comics (GCD and Wikipedia)
items: Next to Comic Vine, Bookcase now also looks in the Grand Comics Database (comics.org) and the Dutch Wikipedia album lists – good for Suske en Wiske, Jommeke, De Kiekeboes, Nero, De Rode Ridder, Urbanus and many more. No key needed.
Shelf ⚙ → Online → Where to look: Comic Vine, then GCD, then Wikipedia (the first list that holds all your album numbers wins), or just one of them. GCD works in the Android app.
The series page shows every album, the ones you don't have grey – also for Flemish and Dutch series. Tap a grey album to see its cover (from GCD) and Find it.
Look up online… and + Add a series have Comic Vine · GCD · Wikipedia buttons to pick the right series yourself.

entries.title: Games: play your own backups (first version)
items: Open a system (like SNES) → ▶ How to play: pick the emulator app on this phone (or "Let Android ask", which works with any emulator) and the folder with your backups. "Look for games" puts the files on the games in your list and can add the ones that are missing.
A game with a backup gets a ▶ on its tile and a Play button. RetroArch starts with the right core; PPSSPP, Dolphin, NetherSX2, DuckStation, DraStic, Redream and others start directly.
Play on my PC: the PC starts the game with its own emulator, or a Steam game. Set the folders and emulators in Nightvault on the PC: Settings → Games: play on this PC (needs the new PC files).
Save to phone: copies a backup from the PC into the phone folder once (a disc's .bin files come along), then it plays offline.
Only your own backups. Some systems need the console's BIOS file inside the emulator (PS1, PS2, Saturn …).

entries.title: Games: a square tile for every game system
items: The first page of Games now has square tiles (like the album tiles in Music) for every game system and handheld: PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo, Nintendo handhelds, Sega, Atari, other consoles and handhelds, home computers and phones.
A tile shows the system's name, how many games you have and the covers of your newest games. Systems without games are dimmed - tap one to add its first game.
"Only systems with games" at the top shows just yours. Never use a system? Open it → ⚙ → Hide this system.

More older systems: Atari 5200/7800/Jaguar/Lynx, Neo Geo CD, PC Engine CD, 3DO, CD-i, ColecoVision, Intellivision, Vectrex, WonderSwan, Neo Geo Pocket, Virtual Boy, Commodore 64, Amiga, MSX, ZX Spectrum and more.

entries.title: New app: 3D Print
items: 3D Print is here (The Nightvault → Apps → install it). Your STL, OBJ and 3MF models with a 3D viewer: turn with one finger, zoom and move with two, pick a colour, full screen.
Add models from a folder on your phone (nothing is copied), copy files into the app – ZIP downloads from Printables / Thingiverse work too – or use the 3D models from the Nightvault PC app at home.
Files in the same folder (or ZIP) make one project tile, with its pictures and print files. Groups work the same as in Music.
Bambu Studio files: the plate picture, print time and grams are read by themselves.
Print log: tap “I printed this” – printer, filament or resin, amount, time, worked or failed. Prints shows your totals. Mark models “To print”.

entries.title: Bookcase: Discover comics
items: New: Discover (Comics → Collection lists → Discover). See the comics that came out this week or this month, or browse every series of a publisher (Marvel, DC, Image …) with a search.
Tap any series to see all its issues - yours in colour, the rest grey - without adding anything. "Add to my collection lists" only when you want it.
Fixed: the "Add a series" search could not be closed without searching first. Tap outside it, press Back or tap Close.

entries.title: Bookcase: see every issue of your series
items: Open a series on the Comics shelf and you see every issue that exists - yours in colour, the ones you don't have grey. Bookcase gets the list from Comic Vine by itself the first time (with your Comic Vine key).
One comic of a series is now enough: it gets a series tile that opens to the whole list, and the tile shows how many you have, like "1 of 72".
Tap a grey issue to find it on your sites, copy its title or mark it as on paper. It is a setting per shelf (shelf ⚙), on for Comics.

entries.title: Bookcase: no doubles, better publishers
items: Fixed: adding a folder that contains a folder you added before (like Torr with the Weekly Pack inside) no longer adds those comics a second time. Doubles that are already there are removed when Bookcase opens - your files stay.
Fixed: a folder like "2026.08.19 Weekly Pack" is no longer taken for a publisher.
New: the publisher in the file name is used too, like (Mad Cave Studios) or (Dynamite Entertainment).
A file that is damaged, not fully downloaded or really a 7-Zip file now says so.

entries.title: Bookcase: collection lists for comics
items: New on the Comics shelf: Collection lists. A list shows every issue of a series from Comic Vine, per publisher - grey when you don't have it, in colour when you do.
Two badges: D = digital (set by itself when Bookcase has the comic) and P = on paper (tick it, or mark many at once like 1-12, 15). A price per paper comic is optional, with totals.
Add a series with "+ Add a series", or "Add the series I have" for everything that was looked up on Comic Vine. A series also shows "All issues" at the top.
Tap a missing issue: "Find it on …" opens your own search sites (Bookcase ⚙ → Find it), or copy its title to search anywhere.

entries.title: New: Nightvault Cinema
items: Your movies, TV shows, cartoons and anime, each on its own shelf, with one video player. Find it as a new tile in The Nightvault (Apps → Cinema).
Add videos: pick a folder on the phone (nothing is copied) or copy files into the app. Names are read from the file names (Inception (2010), Doctor Who S01E05, Frieren - 05) and you check them first.

Your PC: the films and shows in the PC app's Watch collections show up by themselves when you are home. Videos the phone can't play (MKV with HEVC, DTS sound …) are converted by the PC while you watch. Needs the newest PC app files.
Save to phone: ⋯ → Save to phone copies a film or a whole season from the PC into a phone folder, for a plane or camping trip. Remove it again with ⋯ or in The Nightvault → My PC.
Remembers where you stopped (also on the PC), marks what you watched, plays the next episode by itself, subtitles (SRT, VTT, ASS and the PC's), speed, sound track.
Posters, story, film series and episode names from TMDB with your own free key (⚙ → TMDB). Film series become one tile, organised like Music: groups, groups inside groups, pins, Sort by.

entries.title: Bookcase: look up comics on Comic Vine
items: Type your Comic Vine key once (Comics shelf ⚙ → Online). Bookcase then looks up the publisher and series of comics that don't say it themselves, and fills in the story and cover when they are missing.
It asks once per series and remembers the answer, so it only needs the internet while it looks. After adding comics it offers to look them up.
Picked the wrong series? Comic ⋯ → "Look up online (Comic Vine)…" and tap the right one - it is used for the whole series.
Also: guessing a publisher from the name is more careful now, and "previous / next in series" stays inside the same series.

entries.title: Bookcase: publishers for comics that don't say
items: Many comics (like those in a weekly pack) have no publisher inside the file. Bookcase now fills it in anyway: from another issue of the same series that does have one, or from well-known series and characters (Batman → DC, Spider-Man → Marvel, Saga → Image …).
The comic's page tells you where it came from, for example "guessed from the name" - fix it with Edit details if it is wrong.
New on the Comics shelf: a "No publisher" filter. Tap Select → All → ⋯ → "Set the publisher…" to give many comics their publisher at once.

entries.title: New app: Boardgames
items: Boardgames is here: shelves for Board games, Wishlist, and Miniatures & terrain, plus Plays. Open it from its tile in The Nightvault (add it on the Apps screen).
Your BoardGameGeek collection, wishlist and plays come in by themselves every morning (once the BGG user name and token are set on GitHub).
A game and its expansions share one tile. Groups, groups inside groups, pins, tile covers and Select work like in Music and Bookcase.
Each game has a page with box art, players, play time, complexity, BGG rating and rank, your rating, plays and the expansions you have.
Log a play: date, players, scores and who won (★). The Android app sends it to BGG right away (Settings → log in to BGG once); when you are offline it goes later.
Add games that are not on BGG, and miniatures and terrain (which game or army, how many, paint), with your own photo.

entries.title: New app: Games
items: Games is here: a list of your computer, console, retro and handheld games and a wishlist. Open it from its tile in The Nightvault (add it on the Apps screen).
Shelves per platform (PC, Switch, PS2 …) plus All games and Wishlist. A shelf appears by itself when you add a game for that platform.
One tile per game with all your copies inside: digital (Steam, GOG, Epic, eShop …) or physical with what's included (sealed, complete in box, loose) and the region (PAL, NTSC-U, NTSC-J).
Organised like Music: series tiles by themselves (Zelda, Half-Life …), your own groups, groups inside groups, select several, pin, tile cover, undo, Sort by and search everywhere.

Find games by name with their cover via IGDB, more covers via SteamGridDB, and import your Steam library and wishlist. These need your own free keys: Games ⚙ → Online lookup. They stay on your phone only.
Backup: Games ⚙ → Save all my games.

entries.title: Audiobooks: organised like Music and Bookcase
items: Books in a series share one tile (in series order, #1, #2 …); an author's other books share a tile too (Settings → Bundle books by author).

The same groups as Music and Bookcase: + Group, groups inside groups, ⋯ → Put in a group…, Add books…, Rename, Choose the tile cover, ★ Pin, Select several and move them, Undo, and Save my groups in Settings.
Tapping a book opens its page first: Continue / Listen, previous and next in the series, details and bookmarks. Grouped / All books and Sort by on every page; search also finds groups.
The series is read from the files (series tags), from a title like "Mort (Discworld #4)" or from folders (Author / Series / Book). Books added before: ⋯ → Read the book info again, or Edit details.
An author folder with one file per book now becomes separate books.

entries.title: Bookcase: comics by publisher
items: Comics are now bundled by publisher: Comics › Marvel › Spider-Man › the volumes. The publisher comes from the comic itself (ComicInfo.xml), or from your folders (Comics/Marvel/…).
It is a setting per shelf: shelf ⚙ → "Bundle series by publisher". On for Comics, off for Books, Manga and the other shelves - switch it on there if you want it.
Moving things by hand still wins, and you can fill in or change the publisher with Edit details. Shelf ⚙ → "Read the details of all books again" fills it in for books you added before.

entries.title: New: Nightvault Bookcase
items: A new app in The Nightvault: Bookcase. It opens on shelves - Comics, Manga, Books, Rulebooks, RPG and Colouring books - and you can make your own shelves.
Add books from a folder on your phone (nothing is copied) or copy them into the app. It reads CBZ, CBR, PDF, EPUB and folders of pictures, also with WebP and AVIF pages.
Series are bundled behind one tile by themselves, in the right order. Groups, groups inside groups, pins and moving work just like in Music.

One reader for everything: it remembers your page, turn pages by tapping the edges or swiping (right to left for manga), pinch or double-tap to zoom, two pages side by side on a wide screen, night mode, bookmarks, contents, search inside PDFs, and the next volume at the end.
Print the whole book, one page or a range of pages (on Android you can also choose Save as PDF).

entries.title: Music: rename groups, undo, a backup of your groups, search inside groups
items: Rename a group: group ⋯ → Rename. Your own group keeps everything in it; for an artist or series tile only the name on the tile changes.
Undo: after moving, adding, taking out, removing or renaming, the message at the bottom has an Undo button for a few seconds.

A backup of your groups: Settings → Your groups → Save my groups (to Google Drive, mail …) and Load from a file. Your groups, groups inside groups, albums you placed by hand, tile covers and pins come back on a new phone.
Search looks inside groups: matching groups show as tiles, and every album found says where it is (like “in Star Wars › Episode I”).
Behind the scenes: the group logic is now one shared part of The Nightvault, so the other apps get exactly the same groups later.

entries.title: Music: fix - choosing the cover of a group with groups inside
items: Fixed: for a group with other groups inside (like Star Wars), tapping a cover under "Choose the tile cover" did nothing when that album sat in one of the groups inside. It now becomes the tile cover.

entries.title: Music: pin tiles to the top
items: Album ⋯ or group ⋯ > "★ Pin to the top": the tile always shows first, on the main page, inside a group or on an artist page - whatever the sort order. A small gold star marks it.
Pin several at once: select them (long-press) and tap ★ in the bar at the bottom.
Tap "Unpin from the top" (or ★ again) to put it back in its normal place.

entries.title: Music: select several tiles and move them at once
items: Long-press a tile (or tap "Select") and tap more tiles - albums and groups together. They get a tick.
The bar at the bottom: "Move to…" puts them all in a group, a new group or back on the main page. Inside a group, "Take out" moves them one level up.
Cancel or the back button ends selecting.

entries.title: Music: groups inside groups, and add albums from a list
items: A group can hold other groups: for example a STAR WARS tile with "Episode I", "The Mandalorian" and game music inside, each with its own albums. Group ⋯ > "New group inside", or "Put this group inside another group…".
Group ⋯ > "Add albums…": a searchable list of all your albums - tick several and add them at once. It shows which group each album is in now. Works for your own groups and for artist tiles.
A tile shows what is inside ("2 groups · 6 albums"); Play, Shuffle, Save to phone and the totals go over everything inside.
A group name now matches whole words only, and the longest name wins ("Star Wars Episode I" before "Star Wars").

entries.title: Take with me: music from your PC, and save it to the phone
items: The Nightvault > My PC (computer button at the top): connect to the Nightvault PC app over your home Wi-Fi. On the PC: Settings > Phone access > Switch on, then type its address and code here.
Music shows the PC's albums with a small PC sign, in the same library. Albums that are already on the phone show once, and the phone copy plays. When you are away from home, PC songs are greyed out.
"All / On this phone / On my PC" next to the sort menu shows just one side.
Album (or group, or playlist) > Save to phone: as an offline copy in the app, or as real files in your music folder (e.g. on the SD card) - kept for good. WMA/APE are converted to MP3 by the PC.
Album ⋯ > "Keep on this phone" turns an offline copy into a normal phone album. The Nightvault > My PC lists all offline copies with their size, to remove or keep.
Album ⋯ > "Put in a group…": move an album into a group tile (or a new one), or take it out to its own tile; "Back to automatic" undoes it.
Group ⋯ > "Choose the tile cover": one of the covers inside, a random one, changing covers, or a picture from the phone.
"Sort by" on every page: artists, playlists, inside groups and artists, inside playlists and in search results.
"Various" and "Various artists" are now one artist.

entries.title: Music: artist and series tiles, totals
items: Albums now come in groups: all albums of one artist (e.g. Avril Lavigne) in one tile, and compilation series like Thunderdome (Thunderdome 06, IV, 2001, "Various - Thunderdome 2003" …) in one tile. The tile shows how many albums are inside.
Make your own group with "+ Group": every album with that word in its name or artist goes in that tile.
Inside a group, an artist or an album: number of albums, songs, total length and GB, with Play and Shuffle for all of it. The Albums page shows the totals of your whole library at the top.
"Grouped" / "All albums" next to the sort menu switches the groups off.

CD numbers in the middle of an album name are recognised too: "Thunderdome 2008 (CD1) - Early Rave" and "(CD2) - Hardcore" become one album, with the CD names shown on the CD blocks. Your library is fixed by itself.

entries.title: Music: the debug log says Music
items: The debug log now names Music "Music" instead of "Audiobooks" (they are one app underneath).

entries.title: Music: cover names and a clear message when covers can't be looked up
items: Any picture with "front" in its name (front.jpeg, Front.JPG, …-front.jpg, Frontcover.png) is taken as the album cover.
Fixed: a cover was skipped when a word in its name only started like a skipped word ("Disco … Front.jpg" looked like "disc").
When the cover website can't be reached (some Wi-Fi networks, like at work, block it), Music now says so and suggests mobile data, instead of "Nothing found".

entries.title: Music: Covers folders win, better online search
items: A picture in a Covers / Scans folder (next to the songs or in the CD folder) now always wins over the CD picture inside the songs - also with a plain name like 01.jpg. Back, cd1, inlay and similar are still skipped.
Run Settings → "Look for changes" once to get these covers for music you already added.
"Find a cover online" also searches with loose words and with numbers as Roman numerals (Thunderdome 06 = Thunderdome VI).

entries.title: Music: every CD of an album folds open on its own
items: In an album with more CDs, each CD is its own block: its CD picture, "CD 1" / "CD 2", number of songs and length, and a play button for just that CD.
Tap a CD to fold its songs open or closed. They start folded; the CD that is playing is open.
The CD picture comes from a picture in that CD's folder or the Covers folder named like cd1 / disc 1, else from the picture inside its songs (the disc scan).

entries.title: Music: pick the cover from the album's own folder
items: Album ⋯ → "Change the cover picture" now shows the pictures in that album's folders first (the album folder, its CD folders and Covers / Scans folders). Tap the right one.
"Find a cover online" and "Pick from elsewhere on the phone" are right below.
For music added before this update: Settings → "Look for changes" next to your folder once, so Music knows which pictures are in it.

entries.title: Music: CD1 and CD2 in one album, better covers
items: Albums split over CDs ("Album (CD1)", "Album - CD 2", "Disc 2", or folders called CD1 / CD2) are now one album, with Disc 1 / Disc 2 inside. The tile shows "2 CDs".
Your library is fixed by itself when you open Music; favourites, play counts and playlists come along.

Covers: the picture in the album folder (front, cover or folder.jpg - also in a Covers / Scans / Artwork folder) now wins over the picture inside the songs, which is often a scan of the CD. Pictures like cd1.jpg, back.jpg or inlay.jpg are never used as the cover.
To get the folder covers for music you already added: Settings → "Look for changes" next to your folder.
Album ⋯ → "Find a cover online": pick the right cover from MusicBrainz. Settings → "Find missing covers online" does it for all albums without a cover (only when the album name matches exactly).

entries.title: Music: debug log shows how far adding songs got
items: With Debug mode on, Music now writes down when adding songs starts, how far it got (every 250 songs), when the app went to the background, and whether it was interrupted.

entries.title: Music: adding a big folder no longer stops when the phone sleeps
items: While Music adds songs from a folder, the screen stays on, so the phone doesn't go to sleep and stop it.

If it is stopped anyway (phone locked, app closed), the songs read so far are kept, and the next time you open Music it asks "Continue where it stopped?" - it then skips the folder search and the songs that are already in.

entries.title: Music: see what it does while looking in a big folder
items: While Music looks through a big folder or an SD card, it now shows how many songs it found so far, how many folders it looked at, which folder it is in and how long it has been busy, with a moving bar.
A Stop button, in case you picked a folder that is too big. Tip: pick the music folder itself, not the whole SD card.
While reading the songs afterwards, the song it is reading is shown under the bar.

entries.title: Music: first version
items: New app in The Nightvault: Music. Open it from its tile (Apps → install it first if you don't see the tile).
Add → "Use a folder on this phone": pick your music folder. Nothing is copied - the songs play from there. (On the website the songs are copied into the app.)
Albums with big covers, Artists, Songs, Playlists and search. Albums, artists and covers come from the song tags, or from the folder names (Artist / Album / 01 Song) when tags are missing.
Now playing: big cover, shuffle, repeat (all or one song), queue, favourite heart, sleep timer. Swipe the cover to go to the next or previous song.
Your own playlists, plus Favourites, Most played, Recently played and Recently added.
Remembers what was playing and where. Controls on the lock screen, in the notification and on Bluetooth headphones.
Plays MP3, FLAC, M4A/AAC, OGG/Opus and WAV. WMA and APE files can't play on a phone - the app tells you how many it skipped.

entries.title: Audiobooks: chapters of LibriVox books
items: Chapters are now found in M4B files that keep their chapter names spread through the book (LibriVox books, for example).
For a book added before: ⋯ → "Read the book info again".

entries.title: Audiobooks: books from a folder play now
items: Fixed: books from a folder on the phone got the wrong part of the file, so they did not start and their title, author and length were missing.
For a book added before this fix: open it, tap ⋯ → "Read the book info again".

entries.title: Debug mode
items: The Nightvault → bottom → "Debug mode" (or Audiobooks → Settings): the apps write down everything that happens.
A bug button then shows the log: "Copy for Claude" to paste it into a chat, "Share", or "Send to GitHub" - pick which app it is about and that app's chat can read it.
Android: the app's own Android messages can be added to the log too.

entries.title: Audiobooks: books from a folder, second try
items: Books from a folder on the phone are read in a safer way, with a second way to read them when the first one does not work.
If a book still does not start, a message appears with "Check the file": it shows what goes wrong - send a screenshot of it.
About this book → "Read the book info again" fills in the title, author, length and chapters of a book that was added without them.

entries.title: Audiobooks: play from a folder, no copy
items: Add → "Use a folder on this phone": pick the folder with your audiobooks and they play from there - nothing is copied, so no extra space.
Every book folder inside it becomes a book; loose M4B/MP3 files directly in it are a book each. You check the list before anything is added.
Settings → Folders on this phone → "Look for new books" adds books you put in the folder later.
"Copy files into the app" is still there, for books you want to keep after deleting the originals.

entries.title: Updates for every app
items: The Nightvault now looks for updates itself, so you get them even without Scanner installed.
Android: it tells you which of your apps changed, and only asks when something new is there for the apps on your phone (or a new app came out). "Later" hides that update.
What's new and Check for updates are at the bottom of The Nightvault; What's new only shows news for the apps you have.

entries.title: Audiobooks in the app list
items: Audiobooks can now be installed from Apps in The Nightvault (the previous build still showed it as "coming later").

entries.title: New app: Nightvault Audiobooks
items: Audiobooks is now a real app in The Nightvault: open Apps and install it.
Tap Add and pick the files of a book: one M4B, one long MP3/M4A, or all the MP3s of a book at once. They are copied into the app, so they play without internet.
Remembers where you were in every book, with chapters (also inside M4B and MP3 files), bookmarks, speed from 0.5× to 3.5× and a sleep timer.
Android app: keeps playing with the screen off, with play/pause and skip buttons in the notification and on the lock screen.

entries.title: Back button in the binder
items: In a set or a game in Binder, the back button now goes back one step (to the set list, then the game list) instead of straight to the tiles.

entries.title: The app starts on The Nightvault
items: The Android app now opens on The Nightvault: the tiles for Scanner, Binder, Convert and the apps coming later. Tap a tile to open it.
Your collection stays exactly as it was.
The back button on the first screen of Scanner or Binder takes you back to the tiles.

entries.title: Logo screen fits every phone
items: The word Nightvault on the screen you see when the app opens is no longer cut off at the edges, also on narrow phones or with a big text size.

entries.title: The Nightvault: even more apps coming
items: The Apps screen in The Nightvault (test) now also shows Nightvault Cinema, Boardgames, 3D Print, Collectables and Games as coming later.
They can't be installed yet - this is only to show how they will look.

entries.title: The Nightvault: new apps coming
items: In The Nightvault (test), the Apps screen now shows three apps that are on the way: Nightvault Bookcase (books, manga, comics and rulebooks), Nightvault Music and Nightvault Audiobooks.
They can't be installed yet - this is only to show how they will look.

entries.title: The Nightvault: Scanner and Binder tiles
items: In The Nightvault (test) this app now has two tiles: Nightvault Scanner (the whole app) and Nightvault Binder (only your binders, no tabs and no scanning). Both use the same collection.
Opened normally, nothing changes in this app.

entries.title: The Nightvault (test)
items: A first test of The Nightvault: one home screen with a tile per Nightvault app - Binder (this app), Convert, and more later. Open it at brokeuh.github.io/nightvault-pocket/hub/.
When you open Binder from there, a small button at the top left takes you back to the tiles. Opened on its own, nothing changes.

entries.title: Bigger card pictures
items: Cards whose picture on the card site is small are now enlarged to fill the screen in the big picture too.

entries.title: Swiping, part 2
items: The big card picture uses the full width of the screen again; the ‹ › buttons now sit on the sides of the picture.
You can also swipe left and right in the card window itself (before opening the big picture) to go through the cards.

entries.title: Swipe through cards
items: In the big card picture, swipe left or right (or use the ‹ › buttons) to go to the next or previous card of the set - or of your search results. When you close it, the card window shows the card you ended on.

entries.title: Better card search in the binder
items: Searching a name on a game's set list now finds every card with that name in it, in every set: for Magic all Chandra cards and all their printings, for Yu-Gi-Oh! every matching card, and for the other games their complete card list.

entries.title: Find a card in every set
items: On a game's set list, type a card name (like “pikachu”) and you see that card from every set at once, with how many you have. Tap one to add it or see its price.

entries.title: New app icon format
items: The app icon is now a modern Android icon: no more white frame on the start-up screen, and on the home screen it takes the icon shape of your phone.

entries.title: Search in your binders
items: Inside a binder set: a search box for name, type, rarity or number. Several words narrow it down, like “mage spell” or “fire rare”.
On a game's set list the search box now also finds your own cards by name or type - tap one to open it.

entries.title: Start-up screen
items: The app icon on the start-up screen no longer sits on a white circle: the background now has the app's dark colour.

entries.title: Hearthstone screen capture (alpha)
items: Android app, optional: Settings → “Hearthstone screen capture (alpha)”. Binder → Hearthstone → Screenshots then offers “Capture from Hearthstone”.
Hearthstone opens with a floating 📷 button: tap it on every page of your collection (drag it out of the way if needed), then ✕ to come back. The app reads the captured pages straight away.
Android asks to allow “Display over other apps” the first time, and to record the screen each time you start. This is an early test - tell us what goes wrong.

entries.title: Hearthstone screenshots: ×2 and golden
items: Reading Hearthstone screenshots now sees the “x2” badge under a card, and golden copies by their gold frame. Tuned on real screenshots from the Hearthstone app.
Cards that were reprinted with the same picture always go to the same set.

entries.title: Read Hearthstone screenshots, back button fix
items: Binder → Hearthstone → Screenshots: pick screenshots of your Collection in the Hearthstone app and the app recognises the cards on them (golden copies too). Check the list, set ×2 where needed, and add them. Reading the same page twice never doubles your cards.
Android: the back button now always steps back inside the app - big picture, then the card window, then the set list - also after you opened the big picture of a card.

entries.title: Hearthstone
items: New game: Hearthstone. Every expansion is a binder set, with Normal and Golden copies. The card list updates every week.

Hearthstone cards are digital: they count in your collection and binders, not in its value. Instead of a price you see what a card costs to craft in dust, and how much dust the rest of a set or deck needs.
Build Hearthstone decks: 30 cards, 2 copies of a card (1 of a Legendary), one class plus Neutral cards.
Deck menu: “Copy Hearthstone deck code” to make the deck in the game, and “Paste a Hearthstone deck code” from the game or a deck website.

entries.title: Shadowless Base Set and special-print pictures
items: New binder set “Base · Shadowless” next to Base and Base · 1st Edition, with its own Shadowless prices (TCGplayer).
Mark a single card as Shadowless in the card window when you add it (Base Set only).
1st Edition and Shadowless cards now use the TCGplayer picture of that print where one exists. Some of these pictures may still show the normal print.

entries.title: Check for updates
items: Settings → What's new now starts with your version and a “Check for updates” button (also in the full What's new list).
